edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 30 September 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 1 October 2026

items.caseName: Employees State Insurance Corporation v. Sri Lakshmi Srinivasa Jute Mills Private Limited & Others
items.coram: Justice N. Seshasayee (Judicial Member), Jatindranath Swain (Technical Member)
items.headline: ESI dues are trust money, not ordinary operational debt
items.text: A resolution plan that gave ESIC only about 1% of its ₹13.38 crore claim was set aside. ESI contributions are held in statutory trust and stay outside the liquidation estate, even if the claim was filed as operational debt.

items.caseName: Tamil Nadu Mercantile Bank Limited v. E. Santhanalakshmi & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Jatindranath Swain (Technical Member)
items.headline: Guarantor who paid off bank is not a financial creditor
items.text: A personal guarantor who settled the company's bank debt did not become a financial creditor without a formal assignment or substitution. He stood only as an asset purchaser and could not take forfeited earnest money ahead of others in liquidation.

items.caseName: Shri Sant Eknath Co-operative Sugar Factory Ltd. v. Sachin Ghayal Sugar Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka, Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Decide collusion plea before the Section 7 petition
items.text: A sugar cooperative said the insolvency case against the company running its mill was collusive. The NCLT must first decide the cooperative's Section 60(5) application, within three months, before ruling on the Section 7 petition.

items.caseName: Mekaster Finlease Limited v. Prayag Polytech Private Limited
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka, Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Appeal against rejected Section 7 plea becomes infructuous once another CIRP starts
items.text: After Canara Bank's petition put the company into CIRP, the creditor's appeal against rejection of its own Section 7 application had no purpose left. The creditor must file its claim in the ongoing CIRP.

items.caseName: Phantom Studios India Pvt. Ltd. v. Eros International Media Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Mohd Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member), Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: Notice to Eros on Phantom's appeal over NH10 dues
items.text: Phantom Studios challenges NCLT Mumbai's dismissal of its plea over ₹1.48 crore from the NH10 co-production. The NCLT had treated the deal as a joint venture, not a supply relationship, so the claim was not operational debt.

items.caseName: Rajputana Constructions Private Limited v. Rajasthan Land Holdings Limited
items.coram: Reeta Kohli (Judicial Member), Kavita Bhatnagar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Split verdict on blanket immunity from statutory lapses during CIRP
items.text: The Technical Member held that immunity for lapses during CIRP is for each statutory authority to decide. The Judicial Member would have allowed the plea, so the matter goes to the NCLT President.

items.caseName: Phoenix ARC Private Limited v. M/s Cherupushpam Films Private Limited
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member), Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Borrower's CIRP settlement does not free the corporate guarantor
items.text: The Section 7 petition against the corporate guarantor for loans to the Kerala Chamber of Commerce and Industry was admitted. A settlement in the borrower's CIRP does not end the guarantor's liability unless it is expressly released; limitation, forgery and double-recovery objections failed.

items.caseName: VLM Null Group v. The Additional Commissioner, Grade II, Third & Ors.
items.coram: Santosh Kumar Srivastava (Judicial Member), Arvind Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Late e-invoice alone does not prove evasion; ₹63.72 lakh penalty set aside
items.text: The e-invoice was generated only after the goods were intercepted. As the deal was recorded and verifiable, a procedural slip without evidence of evasion could not support the penalty.

items.caseName: Mandalaneni Srinivasarao v. Sri Sai Traders
items.coram: A P Ravi (Judicial Member), Duvvuri Krishna Srinivas (Technical Member)
items.headline: Department cannot appeal restoration orders it has already carried out
items.text: Sixteen departmental appeals against orders restoring cancelled GST registrations were dismissed as not maintainable. The department had already restored the registrations before appealing.

items.caseName: M/s Seafox Impex v. Commissioner, Customs, Noida (and connected appeals)
items.coram: P.K. Choudhary (Judicial Member), K. Anpazhakan (Technical Member)
items.headline: Value enhancement on polyester fabric imports set aside
items.text: Eight reassessment orders fell because the importer's acceptance letters did not carry the contemporaneous import data relied on. Customs must follow Rule 12 of the Valuation Rules before rejecting declared value.

items.bench: Competition Commission of India, New Delhi
items.caseName: Combination: BNP Paribas Cardif / IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company Limited
items.headline: CCI clears BNP Paribas Cardif's stake in IndiaFirst Life
items.text: The Commission approved BNP Paribas Cardif's proposed acquisition of equity shares in IndiaFirst Life Insurance. A detailed order will follow.
